title: Anthropic’s cloud partnerships are getting messy
content:
Anthropic is having trouble securing enough cloud capacity from AWS, Google, and Microsoft, which increasingly see the Claude-maker as a competitor rather than a customer, according to an S-1 filing leaked to The Wall Street Journal.
The leaked filing provides more color to the numbers Reuters and the Financial Times reported in late September, including that Anthropic believes it could spend more $750 billion on cloud contracts, some of which includes deals still in negotiation.
And still, that is not enough. Anthropic is leasing its own data centers and working with third-party data center operators. But the firm worries those operators have a “limited operating history,” which could make them less reliable than the hyperscalers.
Anthropic’s enormous spend comes on the back of an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of the year. The company reported $16.3 billion in revenue during that same time period, with only two customers accounting for about a fifth of sales, according to the WSJ report.
Building on previously reported catastrophic risk disclosures, the filing also warns that Anthropic could be held liable for damages caused by harmful AI behavior to a tune that would exceed available insurance coverage.
Last week, the company told prospective investors that third-quarter revenue alone has now reached $16.8 billion, up 45% from the previous quarter. Anthropic is reportedly targeting a November IPO.
Anthropic did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.

report.summary: Leaked S-1 shows Anthropic struggling to secure cloud capacity from AWS, Google and Microsoft as they become rivals, despite planning up to $750B in cloud spend.
report.background: Anthropic has grown rapidly on cloud credits and capacity from major hyperscalers, but those same companies now sell competing AI models and services. According to a leaked S-1 filing reported by The Wall Street Journal, Anthropic fears AWS, Google and Microsoft increasingly treat it as a competitor rather than a customer, limiting access to scarce compute. The disclosure adds detail to earlier Reuters and Financial Times reports that Anthropic could spend more than $750 billion on cloud contracts, including deals still under negotiation. The company is also leasing its own data centers and working with third-party operators, while warning that those operators have limited track records. The filing arrives as Anthropic targets a November IPO and reports rapid revenue growth alongside heavy losses.
key_points: Cloud capacity is becoming a strategic bottleneck. Anthropic says it cannot secure enough compute from AWS, Google and Microsoft because those providers are also building rival AI models and may prioritize their own products, leaving Anthropic to seek alternative data-center capacity.

Spending is enormous but still insufficient. The leaked filing suggests Anthropic could commit more than $750 billion to cloud contracts, including deals still being negotiated. Even so, the company is leasing its own data centers and using third-party operators, while warning those operators have limited operating histories.

Financials show scale and strain. Anthropic reported $80.7 billion in net loss for the first half of the year against $16.3 billion in revenue, with two customers accounting for about a fifth of sales. It later told investors third-quarter revenue reached $16.8 billion, up 45% quarter over quarter.

Legal and IPO risks are mounting. The filing reportedly warns that Anthropic could face liability for harmful AI behavior exceeding its insurance coverage. The company is reportedly targeting a November IPO, making cloud dependency, customer concentration and risk disclosures central to its investment story.
report.impact: The filing highlights a structural shift in the AI industry: compute is no longer a utility-like input but a strategic resource controlled by Anthropic’s competitors. For the industry, this could entrench hyperscalers’ advantage and push model developers toward costly self-built or third-party data-center capacity. For developers, Claude availability, pricing and latency may vary by cloud partner, encouraging multi-provider architectures and self-hosting options. For regular users, the practical effects could be service reliability, feature delays and higher prices if compute costs are passed through. Anthropic’s IPO ambitions also mean public investors will scrutinize customer concentration, losses and legal exposure, potentially setting a tougher benchmark for other AI startups seeking capital.
report.tools: Watch AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and Microsoft Azure AI Foundry for Claude availability and pricing changes. For self-hosting or multi-cloud fallback, follow open-source tools such as vLLM, Ray Serve and KServe, plus LiteLLM for routing across providers. Company filings and cloud-capacity trackers are useful for monitoring supply constraints.
